output.brief: The rise is mainly a night-shift handling problem inside the DC, not a Haverlow problem. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four (27 July), chilled pallets wait about 3 h 50 min to reach a chamber instead of about 45 min. The dock staging lanes are unrefrigerated and run at 15–17°C overnight, so product warms while it waits. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9%; day shift barely moved, and Haverlow, Pellridge and own-label all show the same night-time rate. Haverlow's trailers delivered at 2.4–3.5°C, so its product was not arriving warm. Its receipt probes read 6.6–7.9°C only because they were taken after the dwell. The chamber air data is also normal. I am fairly confident in this, though I did not check the refrigeration service reports. Separately, Corriebank's self-certified credits may be inflated, but there is no hard evidence yet. Next: restore night receiving to six operatives, set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly from WMS scans, and hold the Haverlow chargeback and volume move. Ask for a claim-level Corriebank extract as a complementary step. Do not drop the night probe.
